incidents.victim: npm / AWS, HashiCorp Vault, GitHub Actions developer ecosystem
incidents.vector: Threat actor (alias 'vpmdhaj') published 14 typosquatted npm packages mimicking OpenSearch and ElasticSearch libraries that auto-executed credential-stealing payloads at install time, including via a stealthier loader that abuses the legitimate Bun runtime.
incidents.impact: Stolen AWS STS sessions, Secrets Manager material across 16+ regions, HashiCorp Vault tokens, npm publish tokens, and GitHub Actions tokens — enabling cloud lateral movement and downstream supply-chain pivoting. Packages were removed by npm after Microsoft notification.

incidents.vector: Token Security researchers chained five SaaS weaknesses — sandbox escape via user code, recovery of discarded credentials, an over-permissive AWS Lambda role, exposure of 1,111 private repository files, and a leaked NPM publish token — starting from a free Zapier account.
incidents.impact: Researchers could have pushed malicious code to every authenticated Zapier user's browser, taken over millions of accounts and the 8,000+ third-party services they integrate. Zapier remediated within three weeks in February; no evidence of malicious exploitation.

incidents.vector: Troy Murray (a.k.a. 'Steve Dixon') operated a seven-year scheme assembling and selling lead lists of names, phone numbers, addresses and ages of elderly Americans to Jamaican lottery-fraud scammers; payment was via wire transfer and pre-paid gift cards.
incidents.impact: More than 22,000 lead lists with personal information on over 7 million elderly Americans were sold, generating $5.2M for Murray and over $9.5M in victim losses. Sentenced May 28 to 121 months in prison plus $5.2M forfeiture.

incidents.victim: Multiple public-software supply chains via GitHub Actions
incidents.vector: In the 'Megalodon' campaign, threat actors injected malicious GitHub Actions workflows via approximately 5,700 malicious commits across more than 5,500 public GitHub repositories to harvest CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials and tokens at build time.
incidents.impact: Mass exposure of API keys, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, SSH keys, Docker/npm/PyPI/Vault/Terraform/Kubernetes tokens and Git platform tokens across affected pipelines. CISA issued a priority alert and recommended rotating all CI/CD secrets accessible after May 18.

incidents.vector: Silent Ransom Group (also tracked as Luna Moth, Chatty Spider, UNC3753) impersonates internal IT staff via phone and phishing email to gain remote-desktop access; if that fails, sends an individual in person to insert a USB or external drive into a victim workstation under the pretext of creating a backup.
incidents.impact: Stolen sensitive legal, financial and client data is exfiltrated via WinSCP, Rclone, Google Drive or OneDrive and then used to extort firms with threats of leak-site publication or sale. FBI advisory issued May 26; group has claimed 100+ attacks, with activity surging in spring 2026.

incidents.victim: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
incidents.vector: Group posing as hacktivists 'Ababil of Minab' breached LACMTA in March 2026; researchers at Gambit Security published forensic evidence on May 26 linking the group to Iran's MOIS, including custom exfiltration tooling and overlap with prior MOIS-attributed activity.
incidents.impact: Attackers exfiltrated transit-system data and then erased databases, virtual machines and storage volumes using both scripts and hands-on-keyboard activity, deliberately targeting virtualization, storage and backup layers to deny recovery. Additional victims included an Israeli media organization, an Israeli university, a Turkish insurance broker and Saudi targets.

incidents.vector: Glassworm operators injected malware into VSCode extensions, npm and Python packages, and more than 300 GitHub repositories using a layered C2 abusing the Solana blockchain, BitTorrent, Google Calendar and commercial VPS providers.
incidents.impact: Botnet had been infecting open-source software since early 2025, stealing credentials and deploying GlasswormRAT on Windows, macOS and Linux. CrowdStrike, Google and Shadowserver took down four C2 servers, severing the operators' access to core infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Suspect exploited an unpatched vulnerability in Ajax's systems in March 2026 to gain repeated unauthorized access; Dutch National Police arrested a 35-year-old man in Buren on May 27 and seized digital storage devices.
incidents.impact: Original disclosure suggested only a few hundred email addresses and limited personal information were exposed, but Dutch broadcaster RTL reported potential exposure of personal data on more than 300,000 registered supporters and over 42,000 season tickets; ticket transfers and stadium-ban records could have been altered.

incidents.vector: Cheungkin (Kelvin) Lam, a former TD Bank employee, accepted bribes to identify high-balance accounts and exfiltrate confidential customer information to outside co-conspirators; separately, he bribed an employee at another financial institution to falsify records when opening fraud-vehicle accounts.
incidents.impact: Insider scheme facilitated more than $3.4 million in customer-account fraud; Lam received at least $155,000 in bribes. Pleaded guilty May 27 to wire-fraud conspiracy and false bank entries; faces up to 30 years at October sentencing.

incidents.victim: French left-wing mayoral candidates (Marseille, Toulouse, Roubaix)
incidents.vector: Coordinated smear campaign used deceptive websites, social-media accounts alleging criminal behaviour and disparaging digital ads against three La France Insoumise mayoral candidates; influence firm BlackCore was identified in marketing material as having capability for such operations before scrubbing its site.
incidents.impact: Paris prosecutors opened a probe on May 27 for suspected foreign espionage, election fraud and online advocacy of terrorism. Investigation involves the specialized national cyber police and consolidates separate probes in Marseille and Toulouse.

incidents.vector: Dutch financial crime agency FIOD executed raids on May 18 against MIRhosting and WorkTitans BV — the entities that had taken over technical assets of EU-sanctioned Stark Industries Solutions — searching three businesses and two data centers and seizing more than 800 servers, laptops and phones.
incidents.impact: Two co-owners (a 39-year-old Russian native and a 57-year-old from Amsterdam) arrested for sanctions violations. The networks were the most-used in pro-Russian attacks on Danish government bodies during the November 13-19, 2025 municipal-election week. WorkTitans customers were told seized data was 'lost and cannot be recovered.'

incidents.victim: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor with administrative access created a public GitHub profile named 'Private-CISA' (created November 2025) and committed plaintext credentials for dozens of internal CISA systems, including AWS GovCloud keys; commit logs show the contractor disabled GitHub's secret-scanning protections.
incidents.impact: Exposed credentials included an RSA private key granting access to a GitHub app installed across the CISA-IT GitHub organization with full read and CI/CD-hijack capability. More than a week after notification, CISA was still rotating leaked secrets; lawmakers in both chambers (Sen. Hassan, Rep. Thompson) demanded answers. Most sensitive material was published in late April 2026.

incidents.victim: Kimwolf IoT botnet operator (US/Canada law-enforcement action)
incidents.vector: Canadian authorities arrested 23-year-old Jacob Butler ('Dort') of Ottawa under a US extradition warrant for building and operating the Kimwolf IoT botnet that enslaved millions of devices — including digital photo frames and webcams — and was rented to other cybercriminals.
incidents.impact: Kimwolf was tied to DDoS attacks measured at nearly 30 Tbps (a record) and to attacks against DoD IP ranges; the botnet issued over 25,000 attack commands and caused victim losses exceeding $1 million in some cases. Butler also commissioned swatting attacks against researchers; faces up to 10 years if extradited and convicted in the US.

incidents.victim: Government of the Northern Mariana Islands
incidents.vector: A cyberattack disrupted the government's email servers; officials did not specify whether it was a ransomware incident.
incidents.impact: Administrative operations for the US territory were expected to slow as a result of the email-server outage.

incidents.vector: A GitHub employee installed the Nx Console VS Code extension, version 18.95.0 of which had been backdoored via a prior compromise of Nx developer systems originating in the TanStack supply-chain attack. VS Code's automatic update mechanism distributed the malicious build silently. Tracked as CVE-2026-48027 and added to CISA KEV.
incidents.impact: More than 3,800 of GitHub's internal source-code repositories were exfiltrated and offered for sale on a hacking forum; GitHub rotated critical secret tokens. Grafana also confirmed it was compromised through the same TanStack incident days earlier.

incidents.vector: An Elasticsearch database was left unprotected on the public internet for at least two months until the server was finally secured.
incidents.impact: Personal information for nearly 19 million customers — including phone numbers, full names and links to WeChat accounts — was exposed.

incidents.vector: Russian disinformation group 'Matryoshka' has been compromising BlueSky accounts since April to repost pro-Kremlin and anti-Ukraine propaganda from established-looking identities.
incidents.impact: BlueSky has been suspending compromised accounts until owners can re-secure them; campaign continues alongside parallel operations targeting Armenia ahead of its June 7 parliamentary elections.

incidents.vector: A bug on the official Trump Mobile website exposed the data of customers who signed up for the company's smartphone; the company allegedly was notified in advance and only patched the issue after YouTubers publicized the leak.
incidents.impact: Customer emails, physical addresses and full names were exposed. Trump Mobile has separately been accused by customers of failing to ship paid-for handsets.

incidents.vector: Group operating under the 'Handala' persona — assessed by the US Department of Justice and external experts to be backed by Iran's MOIS — conducted a destructive intrusion targeting employee devices and manufacturer systems.
incidents.impact: The attack 'crippled' Stryker by wiping employee devices and manufacturer systems. Cited in May 27 Gambit research as part of an established MOIS pattern of fronting destructive operations behind fake hacktivist personas.
